note: Edit the numbers here, then run: python3 tools/catalog-build.py && python3 tools/catalog-upload.py prices. price = multiplier x (sum of parts + packaging), nearest ten, minus one. Each part's cost already includes its packaging (Raushan, 2026-10-04), so several pieces are simply the cost times the count and the packaging table is 0; put an amount there only to add something per listing on top. A part with null has no cost yet: listings that use it keep the placeholder price typed in catalog.json. All figures in rupees. combo_saving: in a pack, pair or set that is not a bouquet, every piece after the dearest costs this share less than bought alone (0.25 = a quarter off); a combo never costs more than the plain rule gives, and one that the plain rule puts at free_delivery_from or more is never priced under it (docs/pricing-plan.md, 2026-10-12). free_delivery_from must match Theme settings > Cart.

parcel.note: PLACEHOLDERS (2026-10-13): what a parcel weighs and which box it goes in, for Shopify's weight and Shiprocket's catalogue. grams are Claude's estimates per piece until Raushan weighs them; the bouquet and keychain boxes are Raushan's (inches: length, width, height), the 'pot' box and the use of the keychain box for hair accessories, charms and tie-backs are assumptions. hsn and gst_percent are generic for crochet until the Meesho listings are read: 630790 is 'other made-up textile articles', 5% up to Rs 2,500 a piece; bouquets may belong under 6702 (artificial flowers, 18%). A variant weighs its parts plus its box. After editing: python3 tools/catalog-build.py && python3 tools/catalog-upload.py weights (and hsn).
